You’ll report to the Director of Product Marketing and own EPM end-to-end: messaging, positioning, competitive strategy, and launch execution.\n\nYou will shape how the market understands credentials security as 1Password grows.\n\n\n\nHow we’re using AI today\nOn the Marketing team, we’re growing our AI capability together and redesigning how work gets done. We’ve built agents to improve workflows focused on competitive intelligence, content creation, and campaign planning, helping us stay sharp, reduce context-switching, and surface the right information at the right time. AI helps us coordinate, execute, and uncover insights faster so we can spend more time on what’s most important: performance, judgement, and driving the future of 1Password.\n\n\n\nThis is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US.\n\n\n\nWhat we're looking for:\n\nExperience and Domain Expertise\n\n - 7+ years of B2B SaaS product marketing, with direct experience in password management, enterprise vaulting, credentials security, or identity security.\n\n - Working knowledge of broad cybersecurity concepts.\n\n - You've repositioned a mature enterprise product. You know the difference between a messaging refresh and actually shifting how the market thinks about something.\n\n - You can market to enterprise IT and security buyers: the admin managing rollout, the CISO approving the spend, and the security engineer evaluating the technical depth.\n\n - A track record of winning in competitive markets by displacing incumbents, not just differentiating in an open field.\n\nTechnical Depth\n\n - You understand how credentials work beyond passwords: API keys, certificates, machine secrets, passkeys, and what it takes to issue credentials to AI agents.\n\n - Working knowledge of enterprise IT: MDM, SSO, directory services, and where password management fits in the IAM stack.\n\nAI-Forward, Not AI-Dependent\n\n - You use AI to go faster, not to think less. You know what to hand off and what to own, and you can tell good output from output that still needs work.\n\n - You want AI to free up time for the work only a good product marketer can do: strategy, judgment, and narrative.\n\n - You own the ideas you bring. Walk into a room with a recommendation and you can defend it. Candidates who produce content but can’t explain the thinking behind it won’t fit here.\n\nStrategic Storytelling and Senior-Level Communication\n\n - You write for multiple audiences without diluting the message. An IT admin and a CISO aren't reading the same document for the same reason. You know how to serve both.\n\n - Strong narrative instincts: open with the problem, build to the solution, and land in a way that makes the reader feel the product was built for their situation.\n\n - You’ve shaped category narratives, not just contributed to them.\n\n\n\nBonus points for:\n\n - Security certifications (CISSP, Security+, or similar).\n\n - Experience developing thought leadership in a fast-moving category. 1Password has a team that produces content. This role provides the point of view.\n\n - You've repositioned an established product category. There's a real difference between entering a space and redefining it.\n\n\n\nWhat you can expect:\n\nOwn EPM Product Marketing\n\n - Own messaging, positioning, and launch strategy for the Enterprise Password Manager.\n\n - Define how 1Password talks about credentials security for employees, service accounts, and AI agents.\n\n - Tell the story clearly to analysts, IT buyers, security leaders, and sellers. The narrative has to work for practitioners and executives.\n\n - Connect EPM’s story to the Unified Access platform narrative.\n\nBuild Competitive Intelligence and Category Positioning\n\n - Own positioning and market leadership claims for EPM.\n\n - Partner with Solutions Marketing on competitive differentiation. Know the competitive set cold: where they’re strong, where they’re not, and how to win against each.\n\n - Track where the credentials security market is moving and keep 1Password’s messaging ahead of it.\n\nEnable the Field with Tools That Actually Get Used\n\n - Produce discovery decks, battlecards, objection-handling guides, and technical briefs that sellers and SEs reach for because they work.\n\n - Take complex concepts like passkeys, machine credential lifecycle, AI agent authentication, and zero-knowledge architecture and make them usable in a customer conversation.\n\n - Surface win/loss signals from the field and turn them into repeatable GTM motions, not one-off documents.\n\nInfluence EPM Product Strategy\n\n - Bring the market's perspective to Product: customer evidence, analyst intelligence, competitive signals, field feedback.\n\n - Make the market case early, before decisions are locked.\n   \n   \n\nWhy join us:\n\n - The credentials security market is being reshaped by machine identities and AI agents. This is foundational work: you’ll help simplify authorization for developers, strengthen access controls for customers, and shape how 1Password governs access as its product ecosystem grows.\n\n\n\nHow we’re using AI today\n\nOur Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security.
